newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crack Peruvian troops storm the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima city in a swift assault ending the ordeal of 71 hostages held by Marxist rebels since December, and leaving all their captors dead. (ALL PAPERS)
- Peace talks between the government and communist rebels have stalled again following a dispute over how to implement future agreements, the government says. (JOURNAL)
- Government negotiators and hardline Islamic guerrillas resume peace talks aimed at nailing down an elusive peace in Mindanao, as their forces battle in nearby hills (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Senate probers ask the Public Estates Authority to justify other lucrative land deals it awarded to private parties at the Manila Bay reclamation area without undergoing any bidding process. (TODAY)
- The Central Bank orders an indefinite bank holiday of Monte de Piedad Savings Bank to contain a bank run and undertake a financial rehabilitation. (MANILA TIMES)
- Congressmen have agreed to revise their proposed tax exemption levels as they try to meet the deadline for the passage of the income tax reform law before the end of the month. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Fort Bonifacio Development Corp will invest over $1 billion for the construction of seven infrastructure projects within the Fort Bonfiacio Global City. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Pure Foods Corp intends to divest from its canned tuna venture in Indonesia, president Renato Montemayor says.
